task.description:
WF-02 Step 1b -- Design gate for REQ-367's design (lib/letflow/design/req367-cd-qa-deploy.md). Claim this handoff (status IN_PROGRESS). Read the design file directly (not just CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary). This is infrastructure design (shell script + GitHub Actions workflow), not Elixir -- apply the same rigor as usual (per WF-02 Step 1b's standard checklist) adapted to this shape: (a) does every REQ-367 acceptance criterion map to a concrete design element -- no TBD/deferrals? (b) is deploy/redeploy-qa.sh's procedure fully specified (each step's purpose, target paths, ordering) without actual bash bodies? (c) is cd.yml's trigger/gate mechanism fully specified, including how it avoids duplicating ci.yml's diff logic, without actual YAML bodies? (d) are error-handling/failure-mode expectations stated (what happens if a step fails, health check fails, etc.) -- not left implicit? (e) are cross-file dependencies listed (what ci.yml change is implied, if any)? (f) is there any actual implementation code (real bash lines, real complete YAML blocks) present rather than structural/procedural description -- FAIL if so, even if a quoted precedent (the real letflow-queue cd.yml, clearly marked as a citation) is present, since that's documentation of an existing file, not new implementation, but check the NEW design sections (\u00a71/\u00a72 for redeploy-qa.sh/cd.yml) do not slip into full code?

One known unusual point to specifically evaluate: the design proposes adding a small artifact-upload step to .github/workflows/ci.yml's existing `changes` job (outside this requirement's own owned_modules of deploy/redeploy-qa.sh and .github/workflows/cd.yml), justified as necessary to satisfy REQ-367's 'reuse the changes job's outputs, no duplicated diff logic' acceptance criterion under a workflow_run cross-workflow trigger. Decide explicitly: is this in-scope scope creep or a legitimate, necessary, minimal touch this requirement's acceptance criteria actually require? State your reasoning either way -- this decision gates whether ELIXIR-DEV touches ci.yml at all in Step 2a.

FAIL immediately on any check failure, no partial credit, per Step 1b's standard hard-gate procedure. Complete the handoff: PASS -> next_action 'Route to ELIXIR-DEV (Step 2a)' | FAIL -> next_action 'Rework CODE-DESIGNER', issues listing every failed check by requirement id. Commit the completed handoff JSON on branch feature/WF02-REQ367-20260917 and push.
acceptance_criteria: Every REQ-367 acceptance criterion maps to a concrete design element, no TBD/deferrals
deploy/redeploy-qa.sh's full procedure specified without real bash implementation bodies
cd.yml's trigger/gate mechanism fully specified without real YAML implementation bodies
Error/failure-mode handling stated, not left implicit
Explicit ruling on whether the proposed ci.yml touch is legitimate minimal scope or creep
No implementation code present in the NEW design sections (quoted existing precedent is fine and expected)

ci_yml_scope_ruling.reasoning: REQ-367's own text mandates gating cd.yml on ci.yml's changes job outputs 'via workflow_run ... or an equivalent that avoids a second independent diff computation,' and explicitly forbids writing a second path-filter regex. A workflow_run-triggered workflow runs as a genuinely separate workflow run and cannot consume another workflow's job outputs via `needs:` (needs only resolves within one workflow run) -- this is a real GitHub Actions platform constraint, not a design choice. That leaves exactly three options: (1) duplicate the diff logic in cd.yml (explicitly forbidden by the requirement text), (2) some other cross-workflow signal-passing mechanism, or (3) the proposed artifact-upload addition. The proposed step is additive only (one new step in the existing `changes` job), does not touch the existing `filter`/`fallback` steps' git diff/regex logic at all, and is the standard documented pattern for passing data across a workflow_run boundary. Given the requirement's own explicit instruction leaves no alternative that avoids duplicated diff logic, this is necessary minimal scope this requirement's acceptance criteria actually require, not scope creep -- ELIXIR-DEV should touch this one step of ci.yml in Step 2a.

issues: REQ-367 check (b)/(f): lib/letflow/design/req367-cd-qa-deploy.md §1 (deploy/redeploy-qa.sh, a NEW file -- not existing-file citation) contains literal, directly copy-pasteable bash statements rather than structural/procedural description only. Evidence: step 2 gives `cd "$APP_DIR"`, `git pull`, `CURRENT_REF=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)` verbatim; step 3 gives `docker tag ... letflow-qa:rollback-$DATE ... 2>/dev/null || true`, `docker build -f deploy/Dockerfile -t letflow-qa:latest .`, `$COMPOSE up -d db`, `$COMPOSE up -d --force-recreate app` verbatim; step 7 gives `curl -sf https://qa.bizdala.com/` verbatim. These are not paraphrased steps ('build the backend image, tag a rollback copy first') -- they are the actual command lines that would appear in the shipped script, distributed through prose instead of a fenced code block, but functionally identical to writing the script body. This is implementation code, not a procedural outline, and is exactly the risk the handoff task told this validator to check for.

REQ-367 check (c)/(f): lib/letflow/design/req367-cd-qa-deploy.md §2 (.github/workflows/cd.yml, a NEW file) contains literal YAML key/value fragments that are directly usable as-is, not structural description. Evidence: the Triggers subsection gives `on: workflow_run: workflows: ["CI"], branches: [main], types: [completed]` verbatim; the job-level gate gives `if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`; the Steps subsection gives the SSH step's four real input keys verbatim -- `host: ${{ secrets.QA_DEPLOY_HOST }}`, `username: ${{ secrets.QA_DEPLOY_USER }}`, `key: ${{ secrets.QA_DEPLOY_SSH_KEY }}`, `script: bash /opt/apps/letflow-qa/deploy/redeploy-qa.sh` -- and the step-level gate gives `if: steps.<read-step-id>.outputs.deploy == 'true'`. Concatenated, these fragments amount to nearly the full real cd.yml body, not a structural outline ELIXIR-DEV still has to design from scratch.

Distinguish from what is NOT a violation: §0's citations of letflow-queue's real cd.yml and this repo's real ci.yml (both existing files, clearly marked as precedent/citation) are correctly out of scope for this finding -- the FAIL is specific to §1/§2's NEW-file sections slipping literal syntax in alongside the procedural description.
